result.builder:
Goal: extend the jsonl-lint CLI to take several files (issue https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/104), in one pull request.

Context: packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js currently reads one file (process.argv[2]), prints `<file>:<line>: <error>` per bad row (newlines in the error replaced by spaces), and exits 0/1/2. packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js exports lint(text). Tests are in packages/jsonl-lint/test/cli.test.js (spawns the bin with spawnSync) and packages/jsonl-lint/test/lint.test.js. CI is .github/workflows/test.yml (npm ci, npm test).

Steps:
1. Do not touch packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js at all; lint(text) must stay byte-for-byte unchanged.
2. Rewrite packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js:
   - Take all arguments process.argv.slice(2). If none: print a usage line to stderr (e.g. `usage: jsonl-lint <file> [<file> ...]`, mentioning `-` for stdin) and exit 2.
   - If `-` appears more than once: usage error on stderr, exit 2 (check this up front, before reading anything).
   - Check each file in the order given. For `-`, read stdin (readFileSync(0, 'utf8')) and report it with the name `-`, i.e. `-:<line>: <error>`. For other names read the file; print `<file>:<line>: <error>` per bad row exactly as the single-file case does today, using the argument exactly as given.
   - If a file can't be read, write `jsonl-lint: cannot read <file>: <message>` to stderr, remember it, and continue with the remaining files (their bad rows are still printed).
   - Exit 2 if any file could not be read; otherwise 1 if any row in any file was bad; otherwise 0. Keep the single-file behaviour identical to before.
3. Extend packages/jsonl-lint/test/cli.test.js (node:test, keep existing tests passing) with tests for: two clean files (exit 0, no output); one bad file among several clean ones (exit 1, only the bad file's lines printed, in order); stdin via `-` clean (exit 0) and bad (exit 1, lines prefixed `-:`) using spawnSync's `input` option; a missing file among good ones (exit 2, error on stderr naming the missing file, and a bad row in another file still reported on stdout); two `-` arguments (exit 2, usage on stderr); no arguments (exit 2, usage on stderr). Also check order of output across multiple bad files.
4. Update packages/jsonl-lint/README.md: usage `node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js <file> [<file> ...]`, `-` reads stdin and is reported as `-`, only one `-` allowed, files checked in order, and the new exit-code rules (0 all clean, 1 any bad row in any file, 2 no file / two `-` / any unreadable file, with other files still checked and reported).
5. Run `npm test` at the repo root and make sure it passes.
6. Commit, push and open one PR on suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test whose body contains the line `Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/104`.
result.verifier:
Run every check at the PR head from the repository root. Each command below is self-contained.

Check 1 — "packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js <file> [<file> ...] checks every file named in order and prints <file>:<line>: <error> for each bad row, as for one file before"
Run:
`d=$(mktemp -d); printf '{"a":1}\n{bad}\n' > $d/a.jsonl; printf '{"b":2}\n' > $d/ok.jsonl; printf '\n{x\n{"c":3}\n[1,\n' > $d/c.jsonl; node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js $d/a.jsonl $d/ok.jsonl $d/c.jsonl; echo "exit=$?"; echo ---; node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js $d/c.jsonl $d/a.jsonl; echo ---; node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js $d/a.jsonl`
PASS: the first run prints `<dir>/a.jsonl:2: <error>`, then `<dir>/c.jsonl:2: <error>` and `<dir>/c.jsonl:4: <error>`, in that order, nothing for ok.jsonl, each line in the form `<file>:<line>: <error>`; the second run prints the c.jsonl lines before the a.jsonl line; the single-file run prints `<dir>/a.jsonl:2: <error>` as before. FAIL: any file is skipped, lines are out of argument order, a bad row is missing, or the line format differs from `<file>:<line>: <error>`.

Check 2 — "A file named - is read from stdin and reported as -; a second - is a usage error (exit 2)"
Run:
`printf '{"a":1}\n{bad}\n' | node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js -; echo "exit=$?"; printf '{"a":1}\n' | node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js -; echo "exit=$?"; printf '{"a":1}\n' | node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js - -; echo "exit=$?"`
PASS: the first run prints `-:2: <error>`; the second prints nothing on stdout; the `- -` run exits 2 with a usage error. FAIL: stdin is not read, the bad row is not reported as `-:2: ...`, or `- -` does not exit 2.

Check 3 — "Exit 0 if every file is clean, 1 if any row in any file is bad, 2 if no file is named or any file can't be read (error on stderr, other files still checked and reported)"
Run:
`d=$(mktemp -d); printf '{"a":1}\n' > $d/ok1.jsonl; printf '{"b":2}\n' > $d/ok2.jsonl; printf '{bad}\n' > $d/bad.jsonl; node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js $d/ok1.jsonl $d/ok2.jsonl; echo "exit=$?"; node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js $d/ok1.jsonl $d/bad.jsonl $d/ok2.jsonl; echo "exit=$?"; node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js; echo "exit=$?"; node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js $d/ok1.jsonl $d/missing.jsonl $d/ok2.jsonl 2>$d/err; echo "exit=$?"; echo stderr:; cat $d/err; node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js $d/missing.jsonl $d/bad.jsonl 2>$d/err2; echo "exit=$?"; echo stderr:; cat $d/err2`
PASS: two clean files exit 0; clean+bad+clean exits 1; no arguments exits 2 with a message on stderr; the missing-among-good run exits 2 with an error on stderr; the missing+bad run still prints `<dir>/bad.jsonl:1: <error>` on stdout (other files still checked and reported) with an error on stderr. FAIL: any of these exit codes differ, an unreadable file gives no stderr error, or the bad file after the missing one is not reported.

Check 4 — "lint(text) in src/index.js is unchanged"
Run: `git diff --stat $(git merge-base HEAD origin/main) HEAD -- packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js` (run `git fetch origin main` first if needed) and `node --test packages/jsonl-lint/test/lint.test.js`.
PASS: the lint function in packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js has no changes relative to the merge base. FAIL: the lint function's code was changed.

Check 5 — "node:test tests cover two clean files, one bad among several, stdin via - (clean and bad), a missing file among good ones, two - arguments and no arguments; the package README documents the usage"
Run: `node --test packages/jsonl-lint/test/` and read packages/jsonl-lint/test/*.test.js and packages/jsonl-lint/README.md.
PASS: the tests use node:test and include cases for each of: two clean files, one bad among several, stdin via `-` clean, stdin via `-` bad, a missing file among good ones, two `-` arguments, and no arguments; and README.md documents the multi-file usage (several files and `-`). FAIL: any of those cases has no test, the tests are not node:test, or the README does not document the usage.

Check 6 — "The change is one PR on suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test whose body says Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/104, and npm test and the test workflow are green at its head"
Run: `npm ci && npm test` at the head; `gh pr view <PR> --repo suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test --json body,headRefOid,state`; `gh pr checks <PR> --repo suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test`.
PASS: one PR on suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test, its body contains `Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/104`, `npm test` passes locally, and the `test` workflow check is successful at the PR head commit. FAIL: the body lacks that text, npm test fails, or the test workflow is failing or missing at the head.

Advisory
- Expected exit codes: check 1 first run exits 1; check 2 runs exit 1, 0, 2; missing+bad in check 3 is expected to exit 2 (unreadable wins), but that precedence is advisory.
- Usage/read errors should go to stderr, not stdout; stdout for `- -` and no-arg cases should be empty.
- Error text with embedded newlines should still be flattened to one line, as before.
- Compare `git show $(git merge-base HEAD origin/main):packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js` with the head file; ideally the whole file is byte-identical.
